## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal text reuse between the *Āsavaduka* and other texts across the Pali Abhidhamma corpus, detecting 201 matching passages shared across 47 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual correspondences occur with other sections of the Paṭṭhāna treating the *āsava* cluster and related dyads, most notably the *Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 2.3; 21 matches, 2,928 shared characters), the *Āsavasāsavaduka* (Patthana 8.17; 11 matches, 2,846 shared characters), the *Kusalattika, Āsavaparāmāsagocchaka* (Patthana 4.4; 9 matches, 1,839 shared characters), and the *Āsavagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.4; 8 matches, 1,768 shared characters) [DharmaNexus]. Further strong structural matches link this text to the *Saññojanaduka* (Patthana 8.20), the *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1), the *Āsavaāsavasampayuttaduka* (Patthana 8.18), and the *Āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka* (Patthana 8.19) [DharmaNexus]. There are no recorded cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora reaching the reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
